reasoning_traces.think:
Temperature scaling operates on the softmax logits z_i through a scalar temperature T, transforming them into calibrated probabilities q̂_i = max_k σ_SM(z_i/T)^(k). This transformation minimizes validation negative log-likelihood (NLL), effectively correcting systematic overconfidence in accuracy-optimized models. The process is equivalent to maximizing entropy under constraints defined by expected true-class logits, ensuring that calibrated outputs reflect genuine uncertainty rather than spurious confidence. In GSE context, this enables precise Kelly bet sizing and informed abstention decisions. For GSI, calibrated probabilities allow robust Bayesian inference and conformal prediction intervals. The method's efficiency lies in its 1D convex optimization, making it suitable for real-time deployment. Failure modes include convergence issues with high-dimensional problems like ImageNet and suboptimal performance on already well-calibrated datasets such as Reuters.
